title: Deprecated ARIA roles must not be used
summary: An element uses an ARIA role that has been deprecated, such as directory, so support is not guaranteed. Remove it or use a current role.
problem: An element has a role value that the WAI-ARIA specification has deprecated, for example role="directory". Deprecated roles may be dropped by browsers and assistive technology, so they cannot be relied on to convey meaning.
whoItAffects: People using assistive technology may get no role information, or different information depending on their software. The structure you meant to expose can silently disappear.
steps: Find the element and its role in the scan result.
Check what the role was meant to express. A directory was a list of links, so a plain <ul> or <ol> already says that.
Replace the role with a current one or a native element, or remove it if the native element already carries the meaning.
Check other pages and templates for the same role, since it is often copied across a theme.
whyItMatters: Deprecated roles are a maintenance risk: behavior that works today can stop working as software changes. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan, then search your templates for the role name. In the accessibility inspector, the element should now show its native role, such as list.
